standard_prerequisites.name: Definition of a well-ordering
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: The unit's Well-Orderings section: a well-order is a linear order (connected, transitive, irreflexive-style structure) whose every non-empty subset has a minimal member
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies minimality and connectedness used in the first paragraph, and the standing order facts referenced thereafter.

core_obligations: Least from minimal (proof lines 1255-1258): a minimal member m of X has no member of X below it; connectedness turns this into m <= z for all z in X, so m is least; uniqueness is immediate for a strict order.
Irreflexivity (lines 1259-1260): the least member of the singleton {a} is a, so a < a is impossible.
Transitivity (lines 1260-1261): for a < b < c, the least member of the three-element set {a, b, c} forces a < c.
Asymmetry (line 1261-1262): derived from irreflexivity plus transitivity as the author records.
proof_roadmap: Convert the minimal element given by the well-order into a least element via connectedness.
Test the singleton, the two-step chain, and combine the two basic properties.
difficulty_reason: A proposition bundling four elementary consequences of well-ordering (statement 1250-1252, proof 1255-1262). Each part is a two-line set-theoretic argument; the whole proof is self-contained inside the span with no citations. H2: elementary but must handle four claims in one proof without gaps.
